title: Stream resume tokens, backpressure handling, and tool-call recovery acceptance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define acceptance criteria for streamed structured outputs that enable safe resume, controlled backpressure, and correct tool/function invocation semantics across hosted and private deployments. Scope includes envelope schema for resume tokens, explicit backpressure signals, idempotent tool-call handshake, error taxonomy, and observability signals required for automated rollback/fallback policies. Out of scope: full UX flows in Console (separate ticket) and billing impact calculations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Envelope schema: Every streamed fragment must be wrapped in a deterministic envelope with flat metadata fields: envelope_version, sequence_index (monotonic per request), resume_token (base64), fragment_type (data|checkpoint|error|end), model_snapshot (model@sha or alias), and optional tool_call_meta. Sample header included in implementation notes.

2) Resume semantics: Clients can resume a stream by presenting the last observed resume_token. Server must replay fragments starting at the next sequence_index. If the token is stale (server no longer has state), service must return HTTP 410 with structured error code 'resume_expired' and a best-effort text summary of emitted content in the body.

3) Backpressure and windowing: Runtime must support a per-request window_size signal in the envelope (integer tokens allowed ahead). When window_size reaches 0, server must stop emitting data fragments and emit a 'blocked_for_backpressure' checkpoint. Clients may set window_size updates; server must resume within 200ms when positive window received under normal load.

4) Tool-call handshake: Every tool invocation emitted in-stream must include: tool_call_id (uuid), tool_name, idempotency_key (string supplied by caller or generated by runtime), input_digest (sha256 hex), and expected_ack_policy (sync|async). The platform must ensure at-least-once delivery when expected_ack_policy=async and provide invocation outcome events (tool_result_success, tool_result_failed, tool_result_retriable).

5) Error taxonomy and fallback: Define three error classes: transient (retryable), partial (some structured fragments missing but overall response usable), and fatal (unrecoverable). Acceptance requires that client-visible final envelope contains 'result_status' in {ok, degraded, failed} and 'error_class' when not ok. For degraded results the platform must provide suggested fallback policy (fallback_to_text|continue_with_defaults|retry-tool) in the envelope.

6) Idempotency and dedup: When a client retries with the same idempotency_key, the platform must return the same sequence of final result fragments (same sequence_index and deterministic application-level result) or clearly mark divergence via 'idempotency_conflict' error code. Tests to verify across hosted and private deployments are required.

7) Streaming termination: Streams must emit an explicit end fragment with final checksum (sha256 of concatenated canonical fragments) and timeline metadata (start_ts, end_ts). Consumers rely on checksum to verify reassembled payload and telemetries must log checksum mismatch events.

8) Observability signals: Each request must emit these telemetry events to the Console: stream_open, fragment_emitted (with fragment_type, sequence_index), backpressure_entered, backpressure_resolved, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_expired, tool_call_emitted, tool_call_outcome. Each event must include request_id, model_snapshot, and region labels.

9) Performance SLOs for resume: Resume latency (time from resume token submission to first re-emitted fragment) must be <= 250ms P95 under normal load for hosted API. If state is archived (resume_expired) server must return within <= 100ms a resume_expired response.

10) Compatibility and versioning: New envelope_version values are allowed but older clients must be able to handle unknown envelope fields by ignoring them; acceptance requires a compatibility test matrix across envelope_version {1,2} and model_snapshot stable/quantized variants.

11) Security and compliance: Tool-call payloads emitted in envelopes must not include plaintext secrets. If a tool requires secrets, only a sealed reference may be emitted (sealed_ref:<kms-id>). Acceptance includes an automated check that flags any envelope containing known secret patterns.

12) Test coverage: Unit tests + integration tests demonstrating resume, backpressure, idempotency, and tool-call outcomes must be present in the PR and linked in implementation notes. E2E test harness must include a flaky tool simulator to validate retriable vs fatal semantics.
test_cases: TC-01: Basic resume happy path: start stream, receive 4 fragments, drop connection, reconnect with last resume_token, verify fragments 5+ are emitted and final checksum matches. Expected: resume_success, checksum match.
TC-02: Resume token expired: simulate state GC, reconnect with resume_token, expect HTTP 410 + resume_expired + text summary fragment. Ensure client can fallback to non-streamed generation.

TC-03: Backpressure windowing: client sets window_size=2, server emits two fragments then emits blocked_for_backpressure checkpoint. Client increases window_size, verify server resumes within 200ms P95.

TC-04: Tool-call idempotency: client replays same tool_call_id with identical idempotency_key; verify single tool execution and duplicate suppression at runtime; if tool returns side-effectful result ensure idempotency guarantee observed.

TC-05: Tool-call async outcome: emit tool invocation with expected_ack_policy=async; simulate delayed success and retriable failure; platform must emit tool_result_retriable then tool_result_success or tool_result_failed and attach to stream with matching tool_call_id.

TC-06: Checksum mismatch detection: corrupt fragment during resume; platform should emit checksum_mismatch telemetry and final envelope.result_status=degraded with suggested fallback 'fallback_to_text'.
TC-07: Security gating: tool_call_meta containing sealed_ref is accepted; any envelope with 'Authorization:' or 'PRIVATE_KEY' substrings must be rejected by an automated preflight and flagged in CI.
TC-08: Cross-deployment idempotency: run TC-04 against Dedicated and Private deployments to ensure behavior parity.
implementation_notes: Envelope canonicalization: use newline-delimited canonical JSON for fragment checksum; sample envelope header string: '{"envelope_version":"1","sequence_index":0,"resume_token":"base64:...","fragment_type":"checkpoint","model_snapshot":"redwood/v2@sha256:abcd..." }'
